rules.selection: Choose the lowest priority number, then listed order, whose dependencies pass.
rules.mutation: Only passes and evidence may be changed by implementation iterations.
rules.completion: Every feature must pass before .marathon/COMPLETE is created.

features.description: Native SQLite workspace initialization and versioned schema
acceptance: bead init creates a valid .beads workspace without touching unrelated files
Repeated initialization is safe and deterministic
Schema creation is transactional

features.description: Canonical native issue model with validated lifecycle and identifiers
acceptance: Model represents required and optional interchange data
Unknown extension fields can be retained
Invalid lifecycle transitions and malformed identifiers are rejected

features.description: Create, list, and show commands with stable JSON output
acceptance: Create commits a new issue and prints only its ID on success
List supports JSON, status, assignee, and explicit limit
Show returns the requested issue in NEEDLE-compatible JSON

features.description: Atomic server-selected claim and release behavior
acceptance: Selection and assignment occur in one write transaction
No eligible work is a successful structured domain result
Twenty simultaneous claimers never receive duplicate successful IDs

features.description: Update, close, and reopen lifecycle commands
acceptance: Status, assignee, and notes updates are atomic
Close retains a required reason
Reopen restores the documented open lifecycle state
Label add and remove are idempotent
Dependency direction follows blocked, blocker, kind
Readiness changes atomically with blocker lifecycle
sync --flush-only observes one committed snapshot
Records and semantically unordered collections are stably ordered
Destination replacement is atomic

features.description: Validated JSONL import with unknown-field preservation
acceptance: Malformed input reports its line and activates no partial state
Unknown fields survive a same-profile round trip
sync --import-only reconciles a valid checkpoint transactionally
doctor performs read-only integrity checks
doctor --repair changes only diagnosed conditions
Warnings and repairs use the required stable prefixes
Capabilities identify contract and store-layout versions
Atomic claim, lifecycle, checkpoint, and command support are explicit
Unsupported profiles fail closed

features.description: Complete NEEDLE v1 subprocess compatibility suite
acceptance: Every required command is exercised as a subprocess
HOME and workspace are isolated for every subprocess test
stdout, stderr, exit status, and filesystem effects satisfy the contract

features.description: Interchange profiles for br-v1 and bf-v1
acceptance: Profiles are explicit and versioned
Every lossy transformation is reported
Fixtures are independently authored or sanitized black-box observations
Migration never overwrites its input
Dry-run validates without activating destination state
Receipt records hashes and transformation counts

features.description: Rapid-fire lifecycle stress and capacity benchmark harness
acceptance: Deterministic workloads cover claim-close, claim-release, mixed lifecycle, and dependency churn without duplicate claims or final-state divergence
Fast verification covers 100 and 1000 beads while the full driver reports every scale from 100 through 1000000 beads

Agent saturation sweeps cover 1 through 200 agents at approximately logarithmic steps across independent, chain, wide-DAG, diamond, and mixed-lifecycle datasets and report frontier, latency, throughput, SQLite contention/write amplification, cache, resources, and highest-supported-agent results
Uncompleted large-scale runs report an explicit resource-limited result instead of silently skipping a scale

features.description: Complete CLI help tree and generated section-1 man pages
acceptance: Every public command, subcommand, argument, option, value domain, default, conflict, and requirement has tested short and long help
bead --help, every nested --help path, and equivalent bead help paths work without workspace access or mutation
Root help and bead(1) explain the intended workflow, ready frontier, lifecycle transitions, blocking semantics, atomic claim, and live-SQLite versus flushed-JSONL boundary
Reproducible bead(1) and per-command section-1 man pages are generated from the authoritative command tree with required reference sections and valid cross-links
Help/man drift tests pass and every expected page plus explicit installation guidance is included in the packaged crate

features.description: Adaptive Git-trackable sharded checkpoints with forensic history
acceptance: Every flush captures all lifecycle states, complete portable bead content, dependencies, comments, structured extensions, and the continuous durable audit-event history

Native checkpoints deterministically switch from one issues.jsonl file to a manifest-backed content-addressed prefix-sharded issue and sequence-sharded event corpus at versioned size or record thresholds
Shard splits rewrite only the overflowing prefix, sealed event shards remain immutable, and interrupted publication preserves the previous verified checkpoint root
Monolithic and sharded imports validate all hashes, partitions, counts, uniqueness, event continuity, and graph semantics before activation and restore to semantically equivalent public state
Checkpoint artifacts are not ignored, sync reports changed Git-trackable paths, and documentation requires an external flush-before-commit workflow without bead-rs invoking Git

features.description: Release packaging, installation, and license verification
acceptance: cargo package succeeds from a clean checkout
Packaged installation provides the bead executable
Apache-2.0 license, NOTICE, README, and provenance ship in the package
